However, as *k* increases, the system is forced to deal with more data points, including those with less commonfeature occurences. Fine-tuning equips the model with the ability to handle the tails of these distributions more effectively, improving coverage for these less common cases. In short, fine-tuning helps the model better generalize to the long tail of possibilities found when sampling a larger number of completions.
